B.title: Update macOS UI reference to “System Settings”
B.description_text:
made changes to rename system preferences to system settings according to new mac os name change

Docs: Update macOS UI reference to “System Settings”

This PR updates the documentation in docs/server.rst to reflect the latest macOS UI terminology.
Specifically, it replaces the outdated term “System Preferences” with “System Settings”, aligning with macOS Ventura and later versions.

What Changed
• Line updated in instructions to disable AirPlay Receiver from:
• "System Preferences" → "System Settings"

Notes
• No issue was created for this change, as it is a minor documentation correction.
• This update does not affect any code or behavior.
• No test or changelog entry required per contribution guidelines for doc typo-level fixes.

shared_entities.guard: File or symbol overlap is a screening signal only. It never implies RT/RI/CC/BC, and it never implies LF (H9).

repeated_touch_evidence.purpose: Evidence support for the LF label only (manual §3.9). Not an LF label.
repeated_touch_evidence.lf_judgeability_reason: Neither patch in this pair declares any touched symbol that this builder can extract, so repeated touch cannot even be enumerated. LF is not judgeable from this packet.
repeated_touch_evidence.exact_evidence_available_for: the two in-packet change sets (A and B) only
repeated_touch_evidence.proxy_limitation: Follow-up history is recorded at path level, not symbol level, so followup_merge_count counts merges that touched a FILE containing this symbol. A merge touching the same file may have changed an unrelated symbol. Therefore `distinct_touch_count_upper_bound_path_proxy` is an upper bound, not a count of touches to this symbol, and `meets_three_touch_threshold_on_path_proxy = true` is a screening signal only. If symbol-level repeated touch cannot be established from the in-packet evidence, annotators must record `uncertain`, never `no` and never `yes` on the proxy alone (H9).
repeated_touch_evidence.window_note: If window_truncated_by_data is true, missing follow-up merges are an artifact of commit-graph coverage, not evidence that the symbol was touched only twice.

temporal_context.screening_definition_of_overlap: Temporal overlap means the two PR branch lifecycles overlapped in the commit graph; it does not mean the two tasks were concurrent agent tasks.

agent_context_summary.reason: These are human-authored PRs. There is no agent, prompt, retry, tool log or failure trace. Treat agent attribution as undecidable in this pilot.

pre_change_test_state.reason: The local clone is a partial clone and the pilot environment does not install Flask test dependencies; pre-change test results were not executed offline.
pre_change_test_state.available_proxy: Upstream CI status is not captured in the cached context payloads.

integration_outcome.note: Both PRs were merged to mainline as separate events, so the recorded integration outcome is 'both landed', not a single joint merge.

counterfactual_pair_merge.note: Counterfactual construction: the two PRs were merged into mainline sequentially, so this merge is not recorded history. It answers 'what would a direct three-way merge of the two branch heads produce', which is the scenario the study targets.

post_integration_tests.reason: No offline run of the merged tree was performed. Absence of test results is 'unmeasured', not 'passed'.
post_integration_tests.consequence_for_labels: AC guide: BC may only be `uncertain` without test or subsequent-repair evidence.

repair_or_revert_history.coverage_guard: The screened commit range ends at data_coverage_end_utc. If window_truncated_by_data is true, the absence of a follow-up fix after effective_observed_window_end_utc is an artifact of data coverage, not evidence that no repair was needed.
